newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian riot town quiet but tense, two dead.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian riot town quiet but tense, two dead.

text.p: The riot-torn Indonesian town of Tasikmalaya was quiet but tense on Friday, with the military reporting at least two dead after a rampaging mob set fire to a number of buildings.
A military official said at least two people had died in the violence, which erupted on Thursday apparently after police had beaten three religious teachers.
Witnesses said the rioters had targeted ethnic Chinese businesses, and also burned down two Christian churches in the town of some 500,000 people, 200 km (125 miles) southeast of Jakarta.
A Chinese-owned Toyota car showroom was burned out. The Roman Catholic "Sacred Heart of Jesus" church, which only opened in August, was gutted, as was the town's Protestant church.
Hundreds of troops moved into Tasikmalaya late on Thursday to quell rioting by some 5,000 people, mainly youths.
"The situation seems pretty much under control, though it is still tense," a witness said. Troops were patrolling the streets and set up roadblocks every few hundred metres (yards).
"A number of streets in the town, where banks and shops were burned, are still closed to stop looting," a local government official said.
Officials said at least 85 people, mostly in their teens or early 20s, had been detained for questioning at a military headquarters.
Witnesses said people had put up signs saying "Moslem" to protect their homes and buildings. They said rioters had scrawled obscenities against the ethnic Chinese on walls.
The rioters had also written signs saying "No to Jesus," "No to the Jews", and "Police are super-corrupt".
